correctness.rationale: The source assumes d_S<d_I and a bounded smooth Neumann domain, positive Hölder β,γ, total N and c=N/|Ω|≥γ(x)/β(x). Set w=cβ−γ≥0. If w≢0, the infected linearization L=d_I Δ+w has strictly positive principal Neumann eigenvalue by testing the constant function, giving R0>1 and existence by the source supercritical theorem; the corrigendum uniqueness proof handles the same pointwise regime. If w≡0, the linearized operator is pure Neumann diffusion and R0=1. The exact reduced steady equation is d_IΔI+DβI(q−I)=0 where D=d_I/d_S>1, q=(D−1)mean(I)/D. Multiply by I−q, integrate Neumann by parts, obtaining −d_I∫|∇I|²−D∫βI(I−q)²=0. Positivity forces I≡q, then q=(D−1)q/D implies q=0, excluding an endemic state. A separate algebraic identity check corroborates the sign factors. No numerical PDE computation is used.
